name: The Benedict (Benedict Apartments)
headline: Archdiocesan Housing, Inc. (Catholic Charities Housing) built The Benedict, a four-story, 34-unit one-bedroom building for seniors 55 and older at 30% to 80% AMI on Midland Avenue in Glenwood Springs, with a 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA; it held its grand opening on 2025-08-07.
why_it_matters: It shows how a decades-old restricted charitable gift (the Benedict Fund, grown to more than $5M), city fee waivers and income averaging up to 80% AMI can make a small 9% senior deal work on a 0.55-acre mountain-town site.

status.label: Open: grand opening 2025-08-07; leasing from late August 2025
status.detail: Catholic Charities reported the building under construction on 2024-11-27 and ahead of schedule on 2025-02-10; Aspen Journalism/Aspen Public Radio reported the 2025-08-07 ribbon cutting and that residents could start signing leases later that month. Occupancy and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not public.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and Catholic Charities reports on lease-up.

background.text: Fritz and Fabi Benedict gave about $2.1 million in the 1990s for affordable housing anywhere in the Roaring Fork Valley; Catholic Charities invested it, it grew to more than $5 million, and several earlier attempts to use it (including two Glenwood Springs sites and one near Basalt) failed before this project.

Glenwood Springs City Council approved Planning File #63-23, "The Benedict" Major Site/Architectural Plan, on 2024-01-18 by a 6-1 vote, with staff conditions and a parking management plan required before building permit; the project used code flexibility for three standards (building orientation, height transitions, planting strip and street trees).

The city requires 20% of units at 100% AMI; the sponsor proposed all units at 30% to 80% AMI for 40 years, with local workforce preference recommended afterward; council discussed but could not guarantee a local-resident preference because of fair housing rules.
Applicant's cost drivers: mountain-town construction costs and supply-chain volatility; cost containment through small units on a small site.
Market study figures in the application: Garfield County vacancy fell from 10.2% to 0.9% over five years; the market area has six LIHTC projects, two age-restricted with 126 units.
An anonymous donor gave $60,000 for custom stained-glass windows in the common areas.

timeline.event: Archdiocesan Housing buys the site for $745,000 (work with the city began November 2021)

Glenwood Springs City Council approves the major site and architectural plan, 6-1
Catholic Charities reports the building under construction, finish expected September 2025
Catholic Charities reports construction ahead of schedule (originally due late August 2025)

discrepancies.text: CHFA gives the address as 2800 Midland Avenue, while Aspen Journalism gives 2700 Midland Ave.
CHFA, the application, the Post Independent and Aspen Journalism describe housing for people 55 and older, while Catholic Charities' March 2024 announcement and Denver Catholic said 62 and older.
CHFA and the application list 34 one-bedroom units, while a November 2024 Catholic Charities post says there would be "a few studios".
The application puts the Benedict Fund contribution at $3,250,000, while CHFA's award description says $3.2 million.
The Post Independent reported 42 parking spaces at approval, while Catholic Charities later described 25 spaces under the building plus 8 to 10 surface spaces.
